subject: Renewal coordination: Anchored ramp + graceband & co-term options
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@starlite.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@starlite.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window and desired structure for 2025

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the partnership this year — Redwood has been great for inference throughput on our real-time features. Our finance team asked me to get ahead of the renewal for our reserved capacity (current term ends 2025-09-30) and to propose a structure that aligns to our fiscal year (calendar year) while smoothing spend across FY26.

High-level ask:
- Move to a 3-year anchored agreement that co-terms to 12/31 each year (so first partial-year period would be pro-rated),
- Start with a 30% reserved token increase in H1 FY26 (phased: 15% for Q1, 15% for Q2), with an option to add burst capacity for product launches,
- Prefer auto-renew with a 60-day opt-out, but finance needs clarity on true-up and proration rules,
- Would like a graceband / bridge credit for the first 90 days if usage overshoots during ramp.

I've attached a short request doc (Starlite_Renewal_Request_Q2.pdf) with our target numbers and the finance team's preferred payment cadence (quarterly or annual prepay). Can you loop in legal / commercial folks and confirm what we can do on co-terming + proration language?

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Product
Starlite.ai

Attachments: Starlite_Renewal_Request_Q2.pdf (1 page)

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@starlite.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window and desired structure for 2025

Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask and the doc. Looping in Karthik (AE) and Marissa (Head of Renewals) so we can get a commercial proposal and a short amendment draft over to you.

Initial reactions / clarifying Qs:
- Co-term to 12/31 makes operational sense; we typically pro-rate any partial first period and can anchor future renewals to fiscal year end.
- For the phased lift: we can model a 3-step ramp (15% Q1, 15% Q2, remaining uplift on co-term date) with committed token bands.
- Graceband: we can offer a 90-day overage credit equivalent to X% of overage spend (we'll calibrate X based on uplift), or a one-time credit pool applied to true-ups.
- Auto-renew with 60-day opt-out is doable; commercial will put explicit true-up sampling and proration mechanics in the amendment.

Next steps: Karthik will build a numeric model and Marissa will draft amendment language + a redlineable doc. Can you confirm the expected annual spend range (ballpark $) and whether you prefer quarterly billing or annual prepay? That'll affect credit sizing.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Sanjay / team — I ran a quick model with the numbers in your PDF. Summary below (high level):

Assumptions: current committed units = 100M tokens/month average. Proposed uplift = +30% baseline on committed units, staged as 15/15 across first two quarters. Co-term target = 12/31/2025 for first sync (so Q4 2025 is pro-rated).

Commercial proposal (sketch):
- 3-year term (2025-12-31 to 2028-12-31 after co-terming),
- Year 1 (partial): pro-rate months to co-term; committed band = 130M tokens/month effective across ramp windows, with monthly true-ups,
- Graceband: one-time credit equal to the net overage up to 10% for first 90 days OR $15k credit (whichever is smaller) — protects against initial overshoot,
- Pricing: blended committed rate with a 12% discount vs on-demand; burst capacity billed at on-demand with a capped per-incident surcharge for launch windows,
- Billing cadence: quarterly invoice preferred (improves cash flow for Starlite), annual prepay available for an additional 3% discount.

Open items we need from your side:
1) Confirm which quarters you want the phased 15% increases to align to (we assumed Q1/Q2 FY26),
2) Preferred billing cadence,
3) Whether you want a canary/burst reserve bucket (we can hold a small burst pool at an agreed rate)

If that all looks directionally right I'll drop a clean amendment and a one-page summary for your CFO to sign off.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
